name: Dial
description: Let clients book appointments around your availability without the scheduling back and forth.
nonGoals: Group events, classes, waitlists, or resource capacity
Additional invitee guests on a booking

Optional tentative calendar display, direct mail decisions and native mobile approval (PAY-007 single and combined price/deposit-plus-fee requests use manual authorization and SetupIntent consent as applicable)
Packages, coupons, gift certificates, memberships (PAY-004; native Stripe payments, deposits, refunds, consented fees, tax and invoices ship under PAY-001, PAY-003 and PAY-005)
Recurring booking series or scheduling polls
Marketplace discovery, ratings, or invitee-submitted reviews
SMS, WhatsApp, phone automation, CRM, campaigns, or marketing automation
Automatic adoption of arbitrary external-calendar time or location edits

externals.why: A connected calendar supplies busy-time checks and destination events. An explicitly not_connected host can still publish from saved availability with a non-Meet location; a configured but unhealthy connection remains fail-closed, and Google Meet requires a healthy conference-capable calendar. The maintained setup journey covers the calendar-optional case at 1440 and 390 pixels.

The prototype's default location is a real Google Meet conference, which requires provider-side conference creation. EVENT-004 also lets an event type use a fixed link, a phone number, or an in-person address instead, so a deployment can run with no event type ever using Meet.
Managed hosting supplies the mail.sender.v1 relay and installation credential. Direct provider credentials are not needed on Managed. No fallback is selected if the configured provider fails.

Direct installs select SendGrid through mail.sender.v1 for sign-in and transactional messages. Managed installs use the RER relay instead. EVENT-006 blocks publication while the selected mail connection is unhealthy.

Existing installations may retain their Resend credentials and mail.sender.v1 configuration. New setup selects SendGrid; an explicitly configured provider failure is not replaced with another provider.

PAY-001: paid event types take payment through Stripe Checkout on the host's own Stripe account, connected by Connect Standard OAuth; bookings confirm only on Stripe's signed webhook. Free event types without saved-card fees make no booking-time Stripe call. DATA-007 asks Stripe to detach saved cards and anonymize known Customers at person erasure, and reports immutable Checkout email as pending with no invented request. Card and payer details stay at Stripe; Dial stores the connected account ID, amounts and Stripe references.
data: event title, duration and USD amount

externals.why: After a committed booking, an event may navigate to the operator-configured HTTPS thank-you page. Only fields explicitly selected by the operator are appended; private answers and booking capabilities are excluded. This is browser navigation, not a server request or telemetry.
Optional host-initiated anonymous sales receipt exports against the mapped income account. Synthetic HTTP-edge acceptance only; no live accounting export is claimed.
data: mapped income account and service item

externals.why: FLOW-005 optional workspace booking notices and targeted erasure requests; synthetic HTTP-edge acceptance only.
data: event title, host time and duration

externals.why: FLOW-005 optional Teams Workflows webhook; URL-only authorization cannot delete posted messages, so erasure reports pending manual cleanup.
data: event title, host time and duration

externals.why: BRAND-001, only when the owner asks (Read website): read the supplied public website, its declared manifest and icon, up to eight of its linked stylesheets and the font file of the face its text is set in, for the booking pages' look; the font file is read only for its family, kind and licence and is never kept, and a Google Fonts family is read from Google Fonts. Public DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com validates every destination and redirect, and private addresses are refused. No key is used.
data: Owner-supplied website URL and the public resource URLs it links
Destination hostnames for public DNS resolution

externals.why: API-002: only an owner-created subscription sends selected native facts to its public HTTPS receiver. Private destinations and redirects are refused. Receiver retention is controlled by the operator; local erasure stops future delivery but cannot recall a payload already accepted. Public DNS-over-HTTPS at cloudflare-dns.com checks endpoint hostnames before each attempt.
data: Booking identifiers, state, time, chosen duration and attribution
Calendar connection health states and named reasons
Routing form, matched rule and destination identifiers
Destination hostnames for public DNS resolution

externals.why: INTEG-006: owner-configured booking measurement only; unconfigured pages and embeds do not load these providers. The invitee privacy notice names Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Meta, Google Ads and LinkedIn.
data: page view, slot selection and booking conversion events

externals.why: INTEG-006: explicitly connected Google Ads and LinkedIn accounts receive confirmed booking conversions. HTTP-edge synthetic acceptance only; provider attribution and account eligibility are not claimed.

MIGRATE-004: only an owner or admin can request a read-only Cal.com API capture with an explicitly supplied access token. The token is used for that request and is never saved. Preview, apply and undo use the saved capture without contacting the source. No provider mutation or live account validation is claimed.
data: Operator-supplied provider credential in an authorization header
Inbound source account, event configuration and booking records

externals.why: MIGRATE-004: only an owner or admin can request a read-only SavvyCal API capture with an explicitly supplied access token. The token is used for that request and is never saved. Preview, apply and undo use the saved capture without contacting the source. No provider mutation or live account validation is claimed.
data: Operator-supplied provider credential in an authorization header
Inbound source account, event configuration and booking records

externals.why: Owner-authorized workflow updates to three documented text properties on an existing HubSpot contact. Unknown contacts are refused; local erasure stops queued effects and retains a manual provider cleanup reference. Synthetic HTTP-edge proof only.
data: Invitee email for an exact existing-contact lookup
Booking reference, state and start instant

env.name: ENVIRONMENT
env.why: Deployment mode: development, preview, or production. Controls local magic-link sink availability and cookie transport security.

env.name: APP_URL
env.why: Canonical deployment origin used in public links; local development uses its loopback HTTP origin.

env.name: SESSION_SECRET
env.why: Hashes opaque operator session and magic-link tokens.

env.name: OWNER_EMAIL
env.why: The setup-supplied identity of the first operator. The operator-auth store persists this identity explicitly and does not create or select a fixture operator.

env.name: SETUP_TOKEN
env.why: One-use credential for first-operator bootstrap on an empty auth store. Its durable bootstrap ledger rejects reuse; this bootstrap is independent of mail.sender.v1 and creates no fixture operator.

env.name: MAIL_PROVIDER
env.why: Selects the explicit RER Managed relay, SendGrid, retained Resend, or loopback-development mail.sender.v1 provider. Missing or unhealthy mail blocks publication.

env.name: MAIL_API_KEY
env.why: Authenticates the selected mail.sender.v1 provider. Missing or invalid credentials fail the provider connection check and block normal or request-only publication.

env.name: MAIL_FROM
env.why: Verified sender for the selected mail.sender.v1 provider; Managed hosting assigns it.

env.name: MAIL_RELAY_URL
env.why: HTTPS relay endpoint for the RER Managed mail.sender.v1 adapter, supplied by Managed hosting.

env.name: MAIL_WEBHOOK_KEY
env.why: Optional mail.sender.v1 SendGrid Event Webhook ECDSA P-256 public verification key for authenticated bounce callbacks. Absent means delivery and bounce tracking is off; unsigned callbacks remain rejected. Sender verification and event publication require the API key and verified sender, not this optional tracking key. Opt in to its deploy declaration and use rer deploy --set-secret to enable signed callback processing.

env.name: RESEND_API_KEY
env.why: Legacy Resend credential retained for installed mail.sender.v1 compatibility. If selected, its connection must pass before event publication.

env.name: RESEND_FROM_EMAIL
env.why: Verified no-reply sender used by the mail.sender.v1 adapter for magic links and transactional messages.

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID
env.why: Identifies the calendar.provider.v2 Google OAuth client. Without OAuth client configuration, the host cannot connect Google Calendar; an explicitly not_connected host can still publish from saved availability with a non-Meet location. A configured but unhealthy connection remains fail-closed; live OAuth acceptance is separate.

env.name: GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates the calendar.provider.v2 Google OAuth client during authorisation and token refresh. Missing OAuth credentials prevent a healthy connected-calendar setup; explicit not_connected publication remains available from saved availability with a non-Meet location, while a configured but unhealthy connection fails closed. Google Meet requires a healthy conference-capable calendar.

env.name: CALENDAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates calendar.provider.v2 push callbacks when a Google Calendar is connected. Without it, callbacks are rejected and connected-calendar health checks cannot succeed; this does not block the explicit not_connected saved-availability/non-Meet publication path. Live callback behavior requires separate acceptance.

env.name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
env.why: PAY-001 (external stripe): the operator's Stripe platform secret key. It exchanges the Connect Standard OAuth code, creates and expires Checkout Sessions on the host's connected account and revokes access on disconnect. Without the Stripe trio, paid event types fail closed with payments_not_configured and free event types are unchanged.

env.name: STRIPE_CONNECT_CLIENT_ID
env.why: PAY-001 (external stripe): the platform's Stripe Connect client ID (ca_…) used to start Connect Standard OAuth and to revoke a connected account.

env.name: STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: PAY-001 (external stripe): the signing secret (whsec_…) of the Connect webhook endpoint at /api/webhooks/stripe. A booking confirms only on Stripe's signed checkout.session.completed or payment_intent.succeeded; an unsigned or mis-signed event returns 401 and changes nothing.

env.name: RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET
env.why: Authenticates mail.sender.v1 Resend delivery and bounce callback signatures.

env.name: IDENTITY_PROVIDER
env.why: Optional Auth installation URL for the oidc-provider@1 setup dependency. Empty keeps email-link sign-in through mail.sender.v1.

env.name: QBO_CLIENT_ID
env.why: PAY-006 (external quickbooks-online): QuickBooks Online OAuth application ID for the optional accounting export destination.

env.name: QBO_CLIENT_SECRET
env.why: PAY-006 (external quickbooks-online): QuickBooks Online OAuth client secret. Stored only as deployment configuration; accounting credentials never travel in an archive.

env.name: QBO_ENVIRONMENT
env.why: PAY-006 (external quickbooks-online): production (the default) or sandbox. Selects only the QuickBooks Online accounting API base; Intuit development keys reach only sandbox companies, at sandbox-quickbooks.api.intuit.com. Any other value fails runtime configuration naming this variable.

env.name: SLACK_CLIENT_ID
env.why: FLOW-005 (external slack): optional operator-held Slack OAuth application ID.

env.name: SLACK_CLIENT_SECRET
env.why: FLOW-005 (external slack): optional operator-held Slack OAuth application secret. Bot credentials are sealed and excluded from archives.

operatingCost.basis: One host and operator, 1,000 unchanged bookings per month, four to six transactional emails per booking including the default reminders when both offsets apply (4,000–6,000 sends/month), with Google Calendar and Cloudflare usage inside the stated allowances.
operatingCost.notes: Twilio SendGrid Essentials 50k was $19.95/month on 2026-10-14; 4,000–6,000 sends use 8–12% of its 50,000 monthly allowance. The low estimate assumes the full Cloudflare runtime fits available free allowances. The typical estimate adds $5/month for Cloudflare Workers Paid, conditional on all metered use staying within included allowances; an owner already paying for that Cloudflare account may incur no additional $5 for Dial. Google Calendar standard use and first-tier R2 usage are assumed within their published free allowances. Estimates exclude overages, domains, taxes, optional tools and paid Google Workspace. The SendGrid trial is limited to 60 days and 100 emails/day, so it is not recurring free service. Extra operators, sign-ins, requests, changes, late Meet links, retries and alerts increase mail volume.
